purpose: Add compact, source-exact R. A. Torrey quotations and illustrations from the verified 1907 public-domain edition of Anecdotes and Illustrations.

defaults.author: R. A. Torrey
defaults.rightsBasis: The 1907 edition predates the 2026 U.S. public-domain cutoff; Internet Archive identifies the item as not in copyright, and each compact excerpt was matched against the stored edition.

entries.title: Fishing for souls
entries.text: It is a good thing to have deacons that go fishing on Sunday — fishing for souls.
entries.sourceLocator: A Deacon Who Went Fishing on Sunday, page 7
entries.recommendedUse: Use the wordplay as a brief opening for a lesson on personal evangelism and bringing people under the preaching of the Gospel.
entries.reviewNote: The title is playful; establish the duty and manner of evangelism from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: The joy of bringing others to Christ
entries.text: There is no joy like the joy of saving men and it is possible for every child of God, no matter how humble nor how ungifted, to have this joy.
entries.slideText: There is no joy like the joy of saving men
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed encouragement to ordinary believers who fear they are not gifted enough to witness.
entries.reviewNote: Torrey's phrase 'saving men' describes participation in Gospel witness; salvation belongs to the Lord.

entries.title: The angry father and the rotten eggs
entries.text: He got a basket of rotten eggs, and went up on the top of an adjoining building to throw the eggs at us as we held the meeting.
entries.recommendedUse: Retell briefly when preaching that an opponent is not beyond the reach of God's Word and conviction.
entries.reviewNote: This is Torrey's reported experience. Do not promise that every opponent will respond in the same way.

entries.title: The first sober Christmas
entries.text: This is the first sober Christmas that I have spent in ten years. Jesus Christ has saved me.
entries.slideText: This is the first sober Christmas that I have spent in ten years.
entries.sourceLocator: First Sober Christmas in Ten Years, page 37
entries.recommendedUse: Use as a short historical testimony of a changed life after reading the governing Scripture.
entries.reviewNote: This testimony must not be used as a universal timetable for deliverance or as a substitute for pastoral and medical care.

entries.title: Give me back my tears
entries.text: He saw that his power was gone and he went to God and prayed, " Oh, God, give me back my tears,"
entries.slideText: Oh, God, give me back my tears
entries.sourceLocator: Give Me Back My Tears, page 54
entries.recommendedUse: Use Colonel Clarke's prayer as a picture of recovering compassion for people rather than merely improving delivery.
entries.reviewNote: Emotion alone is not spiritual power; keep the illustration under the cited KJV passages and the work of God.

entries.title: Conquered by compassion
entries.text: I saw a tear rolling down his cheeks.
entries.slideText: I saw a tear rolling down his cheeks.
entries.recommendedUse: Use to show how sincere compassion may reach a hardened hearer when argument alone has not.
entries.reviewNote: This is a reported testimony, not a technique or guarantee. Keep Christ and Scripture central.

entries.title: Five cents given in need
entries.text: I thought of my seven cents in my pocket, all the money I had, but I went to the front end of the car and dropped five cents in the box and relieved the young woman's embarrassment. I felt no poorer.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as a brief picture of noticing another person's need and giving without public display.
entries.reviewNote: Do not turn the later gift in Torrey's story into a guaranteed financial-return formula; teach giving from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: Have a tract
entries.text: The young farmer boy was not phased in the least. " Oh," he said smiling, " I have seen one of those before. Have a tract."
entries.slideText: I have seen one of those before. Have a tract.
entries.sourceLocator: I Have Seen One of Those Before, page 58
entries.recommendedUse: Use carefully as a historical picture of calm courage in witness.
entries.reviewNote: Do not encourage reckless confrontation; teach boldness together with wisdom, lawfulness, and care for safety.
